questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these endpoints apply updates to an appointment resource? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two front-desk clients both GET appointment A (ETag "3") and then each send a PATCH with `If-Match: "3"`. What happens?
choices: Both succeed and the second write silently overwrites the first
The first succeeds with ETag "4"; the second gets 412 because the version no longer matches
The second gets 409 because the appointment is already being edited
Both get 412 because If-Match must use weak ETags

questions.prompt: A mobile client retries `POST /appointments/:id/cancellation` after a network timeout, and the first attempt actually succeeded. What does the retry return?
choices: 409, because the appointment is no longer booked
201, because a new cancellation sub-resource is created

questions.prompt: Why does the router model cancellation as `POST /appointments/:id/cancellation` instead of letting clients PATCH `status` to "cancelled"?
choices: Because Express cannot route PATCH requests with a body
Because PATCH responses cannot carry an ETag header
Because cancellation needs to create a new appointment id
Because status is not in EDITABLE, so the state transition has its own endpoint with its own rules (only from booked, repeat is a no-op)
